planting.note: Direct-sow seed 1/4 inch deep into fertile, well-drained soil in early spring or, better, six to eight weeks before the first fall frost, since this deep-red mizuna holds its color and mild flavor best in cool weather.

directions: Direct-sow seed 1/4 inch deep into fertile, well-drained soil in early spring or, better, six to eight weeks before the first fall frost, since this deep-red F1 mizuna holds its uniform maroon color and mild, non-bitter flavor best in cool weather. Thin seedlings to allow the deeply serrated, feathery leaves room to form their signature vase-shaped rosette, and harvest whole heads or individual leaves for cut-and-come-again picking. Its consistent color on both leaf surfaces makes it popular for baby-leaf salad mixes, garnishes, and mixed ornamental plantings as well as stir-fries.

planting.note: Direct-sow seed 1/2 inch deep into deeply worked, stone-free soil, thinning to a wide final spacing so the roots can size up without forking; also sowable in late summer for a fall crop.

directions: Direct-sow seed 1/2 inch deep into deeply worked, stone-free soil, thinning to a wide final spacing so the smooth white Minowase-type roots can size up without forking. April Cross is prized among daikon growers for its unusually strong resistance to bolting, which lets it be sown earlier in spring than most daikon types without running to seed. Roots stay tender, mild, and non-pithy even when left in the ground to reach full size, making them well suited to fresh eating, pickling, and simmered dishes.

planting.note: Direct-sow seed 1/4 inch deep in fertile soil and thin to stand so the thick, tender flowering stalks can develop; also direct-sown in early spring after last frost.

directions: Direct-sow seed 1/4 inch deep in fertile soil and thin to stand so the thick, tender flowering stalks can develop; Green Lance is a hybrid Chinese broccoli bred for better heat tolerance than older gai lan strains, letting it be sown over a longer window without bolting prematurely. Harvest the central stalk with its small cluster of unopened flower buds once it reaches pencil thickness, then continue cutting side shoots for several more weeks. The mildly bitter, broccoli-like stems and leaves are classically blanched and stir-fried with garlic and oyster sauce.

planting.note: Direct-sow seed 1/4 inch deep in rich, moisture-retentive soil; repeat-sow every two to three weeks through summer and into fall for a steady supply.

directions: Direct-sow seed 1/4 inch deep in rich, moisture-retentive soil and thin young plants for baby-leaf harvest or wider spacing for bunching-size heads; Summerfest is an upright hybrid komatsuna bred specifically for heat and disease tolerance, so it can be sown through the warmer months when standard mustard spinach types would bolt. The smooth, spinach-like dark-green leaves and pale stems have a mild flavor that holds up well in stir-fries, soups, and quick braises. Successive small sowings every two to three weeks keep a steady supply of tender greens.

planting.note: Direct-sow seed 1/4 inch deep and thin to a close final spacing; also sown in early spring after last frost.

directions: Direct-sow seed 1/4 inch deep and thin to a close final spacing, since Ching-Chiang forms a compact, vase-shaped baby Shanghai-type plant with pale-green, spoon-shaped petioles and medium-green leaves. This variety is notably tolerant of heat, rain, cold, and dampness, which makes it more forgiving than many pak choi types for both early spring and late summer sowings. Harvest whole plants at about 6 inches tall for tender stir-fry and soup greens with a mild, sweet flavor.
